mcqs.q: Among 96 heartworm-positive dogs in southeast Missouri, what proportion of D. immitis isolates had a macrocyclic-lactone-resistant genotype?
mcqs.e: 91 of 96 (94.8%) isolates genotyped as resistant.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about heartworm management given the genotype findings?
o: Current ML protocols remain fully adequate
Resistance is confined to the southern Delta only
ML dosing should simply be doubled
mcqs.e: Rising resistance indicates the prevention/treatment approach should be reconsidered with new measures.

mcqs.q: Which method was used to detect resistance-associated genetic markers in the isolates?
mcqs.e: MiSeq technology sequenced markers associated with ML susceptibility/resistance.

mcqs.q: Compared with superficial skin scrapings, how did real-time PCR perform for detecting Demodex gatoi?
o: Scrapings were far more sensitive than PCR
PCR detected most positives that scrapings missed
mcqs.e: Nine of ten positive cats were PCR-positive with negative scrapings, showing scrapings are insensitive.

mcqs.q: What clinical-relevance point did the study emphasize about D. gatoi-positive cats?
o: Asymptomatic cats can be a source of infection
Only severely pruritic cats carry the mite
mcqs.e: Only 1 of 10 positives had lesions, so asymptomatic cats represent an infection source.

mcqs.q: What outcome followed a single topical fluralaner-plus-moxidectin application in rabbits with sarcoptic mange?
o: 100% mite eradication and lesion resolution within 21 days
Relapse in most cases by 90 days
mcqs.e: A single spot-on dose achieved 100% eradication and complete lesion resolution within 21 days.

mcqs.q: Was recurrence observed during follow-up after the single treatment?
o: No recurrence in followed rabbits up to 6 months
mcqs.e: No recurrence was seen at 90 days, and followed cases stayed clear up to six months.

mcqs.q: By which day post-therapy were all rabbits parasitologically negative for S. scabiei after a single oral fluralaner dose?
mcqs.e: All rabbits tested negative for S. scabiei on day 45 post-therapy.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about a single 25 mg/kg oral fluralaner dose for severe rabbit mange?
o: It was effective without additional medications
mcqs.e: A single oral dose was effective with no additional topical or systemic medication needed.

mcqs.q: Which parasite was most commonly detected by coproantigen testing in the stray/untreated dogs studied in Ireland?
mcqs.e: Giardia duodenalis was most common in dogs at 26%.

mcqs.q: Which parasite was most prevalent in the cats sampled?
mcqs.e: Ascarids were most common in cats at 23.2%.

mcqs.q: Which age groups had the highest overall parasite prevalence?
mcqs.e: Adolescent dogs (<3 yr) and kittens (<1 yr) had the highest prevalence.

mcqs.q: Given that T. gondii prevalence was lower in cats than in their owners, what did the authors conclude?
o: Close cat contact has limited impact on human toxoplasmosis
Cats are the dominant source of owner infection
Household cats pose the greatest risk
mcqs.e: Lower feline than owner prevalence indicated limited impact of cat contact on human toxoplasmosis.

mcqs.q: How did Toxocara cati prevalence compare between stray and household cats?
o: High in stray cats and absent in household cats
mcqs.e: T. cati was found in 47% of stray cats but in no household cats.

mcqs.q: How did coproantigen testing affect detection of Dipylidium caninum compared with fecal flotation alone?
o: It only worked in pet dogs
mcqs.e: Coproantigen increased D. caninum detection several fold over flotation.

mcqs.q: How did D. caninum infection in shelter dogs compare with pet dogs?
o: More common in shelter dogs (adjusted OR ~4.9)
mcqs.e: Shelter dogs had nearly five-fold higher odds (adjusted OR 4.91) than pet dogs.

mcqs.q: What overall recommendation did the data support?
o: Use multiple laboratory methods to enhance diagnosis
Treat all dogs empirically without testing
mcqs.e: Findings supported combining methods (coproantigen plus flotation) for better detection.

mcqs.q: What is the central message of this review regarding non-Dirofilaria cutaneous filarioid nematodes in US dogs?
o: They are likely underdiagnosed and warrant broader surveillance
mcqs.e: The review alerts that cutaneous filarioids beyond D. immitis are likely underdiagnosed, needing surveillance.

mcqs.q: Which skin-dwelling filarioid was highlighted for its zoonotic potential?
mcqs.e: Increased interest in skin microfilariae was driven by the zoonotic Onchocerca lupi.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about the fecal microbiome in diarrheic versus nondiarrheic dogs with giardiasis?
o: Microbial composition was similar; giardiasis was not marked by prominent dysbiosis
Microbiome diversity collapsed in all infected dogs
mcqs.e: Symptomatic and asymptomatic dogs had similar microbiomes; giardiasis was not characterized by prominent dysbiosis.

mcqs.q: Among male dogs, which genus was more abundant in diarrheic than nondiarrheic giardiasis cases?
mcqs.e: Clostridium (and C. spiroforme) abundance was higher in diarrheic males.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about relapse in adult-onset canine neosporosis?
o: Relapse can occur even in dogs that respond completely
mcqs.e: Relapse was common and could occur even among dogs with complete initial response.

mcqs.q: Which laboratory abnormality was prominent in most affected dogs?
mcqs.e: Serum CK was markedly increased (median 3369 U/L) in most dogs.

mcqs.q: Approximately what proportion of dogs were alive 6 months after onset of clinical signs?
mcqs.e: Thirteen of 21 dogs (62%) were alive after 6 months.

mcqs.q: Which large Babesia species is the most prevalent globally according to this review?
mcqs.e: B. vogeli is the most prevalent large Babesia worldwide due to its wide vector range and mild infections.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was identified as a risk factor for large Babesia infection?
o: Living in kennels or animal shelters
mcqs.e: Rural living, kennels/shelters, tick infestation, and lack of acaricide treatment were key risk factors.

mcqs.q: What abnormality was present in nearly all of the 12 dogs with Trypanosoma cruzi infection?
mcqs.e: Eleven of 12 dogs had cardiac abnormalities.

mcqs.q: What did the survey reveal about North American veterinary cardiologists' knowledge of Chagas disease?
o: Knowledge was limited in about half of respondents
mcqs.e: Self-reported knowledge was limited in 49%, and 69% wanted learning resources.

mcqs.q: What was the key clinical message of the study?
o: T. cruzi cannot occur outside Texas
Awareness of Chagas disease should be raised, including in nonendemic areas
Chagas disease in dogs is untreatable so testing is pointless
mcqs.e: Dogs may be encountered in nonendemic areas, underscoring the need for greater Chagas awareness.
